title: JavaScript Functional Programming Core Check
description: Check your understanding of pure functions, side effects, immutability, higher-order functions, array transformations, currying, composition, reduce, and recursion.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: A function that returns the same output for the same input and has no side effects
A function that always logs to the console
A function that can only be written with arrow syntax
A function that mutates its arguments

questions.explanation: Pure functions are predictable: same input, same output, and no side effects.

options.text: Changing a variable outside the function
Creating a local variable inside a function
Passing an argument to a function

questions.explanation: Changing external state is a side effect.

options.text: Creating updated copies instead of changing existing data directly

questions.explanation: Immutable updates keep the original value unchanged and return a new updated value.

options.text: No, it prevents reassignment of the variable, not mutation of object properties
Yes, all properties are deeply frozen

questions.explanation: `const` protects the binding. Object properties can still be changed unless other measures are used.

options.text: A function that accepts a function, returns a function, or both
A function with more than 100 lines
A function that can only run in the browser
A function that must be async

questions.explanation: Higher-order functions work with other functions as values.

questions.prompt: Which array method is best for transforming every item into a new value?
questions.explanation: `map()` transforms every item and returns a new array of the same length.

questions.prompt: Which array method is best for keeping only items that match a condition?
questions.explanation: `filter()` returns a new array containing only items whose callback returns true.

questions.prompt: Which array method is best for combining many values into one result?
questions.explanation: `reduce()` combines an array into a single result, such as a total or lookup object.

options.text: Transforming a multi-argument function into a chain of single-argument functions
Sorting an array without mutating it

questions.explanation: A curried function receives arguments across multiple calls, such as `add(2)(3)`.

options.text: Combines functions so the output of one becomes the input of another
Deletes all functions from an object

questions.explanation: Composition builds larger behavior by connecting small functions.

questions.prompt: What does a recursive function do?
questions.explanation: Recursion means a function calls itself, usually until a base case is reached.

questions.prompt: Why does a recursive function need a base case?
questions.explanation: Without a base case, recursion may continue until the call stack overflows.
